basis: The anonymous family recollection printed by Faris on p.9 explicitly gives James Glasgow, husband of Margaret Rutherford, four sons: William, Robert, James who settled near Moneymore, and Samuel who went to America, plus daughter Ellen. The letter-defined father is the family role represented by James-1025. These are specific named relationships, substantially stronger than the contributed-tree and locality summaries used by the earlier percentages. The same full-letter tradition was already read on 20 October; actual Faris pages now confirm its full structure. Its reproduction by Albert Rutherford and Faris’s pedigree are dependent presentations, not independent witnesses.
limitations: These are probable, not confident, relationships reconstructed from an anonymous retrospective family recollection, with no newly inspected parent register. The original letter remains uninspected. Faris calls the anonymous recollection file5 within PRONI T1959, while Rutherford’s reproduced copy cites T1959/3; retain this reference discrepancy pending archive checking. The 1759 probate index says Drumcarn and names no kin; neither that testator nor the inherited life dates are identified by this reassessment. The letter calls William eldest although the imported sibling birth estimates put him later; those estimates remain unverified. Faris also flags Samuel’s infant daughter and surviving mother-in-law in1824 against the supposed early paternal death. Those tensions require testing, not automatic exclusion. Preserve all existing people, vital fields, maternal grades and alternatives. No Scottish migration, identity merge, live edit or new father attachment is claimed.
scope: Father James-1025, specifically the James/Margaret Rutherford family-account role: James-1024 18%→78%, Samuel-1492 23%→76%, Robert-2425 18%→77%, William-2426 46%→84%, all now probable. The American Robert-12/Arthur-649/Joseph-1543 father grades remain35%, John-4027 remains30%, Mary-4030 remains22%; James-1025’s own William-1026 father remains32%.
source: Faris, The Glasgow Family of Adams County, Ohio (1990), printed pp.8–12, DGS007834162, images1564–1566, inspected23October2026; reassessed24October. Original Chester County estate7520, will17May1824, proved31May1824, portal Doc773006 pp588–589, previously visually read in the project on23October; that reading is reused, not a new inspection.

prior.basis: The proposed c.1700/c.1722 generation is biologically ordinary and the inherited accounts concern the same wider Tyrone–south Derry family investigation. That is a somewhat more coherent local hypothesis than the unbridged Scottish William route. Nevertheless, the apparent father generation rests on the pedigree itself: Faris names Robert's father James of Moneymore, not that man's father; the 1759 index supplies no kin or age; the 1740/1766 households do not identify either profile. The 18% estimate retains modest weight for a compatible inherited local pedigree but incorporates the material possibility that the two James accounts duplicate one adult rather than represent father and son. It is an individual subjective assessment, not a bucket midpoint.
